questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The prize was awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford.
The prize was awarded to Robert E. Hall and to Michael Woodford.
The prize was awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford was honoured.
The prize was awarded to Robert E. Hall, Michael Woodford was awarded.
questions.e: Parallel proper nouns; (B) adds an unneeded 'to', (C) and (D) break parallelism.

questions.subject: CR
questions.q: The GST Council raised the prosecution threshold from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore. Which most strengthens the decision?
o: Cases involving evasion below ₹5 crore are rare
questions.e: Only (A) addresses the rationale; the rest are neutral.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was announced on:
questions.e: Winners: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The committee raised the repo rate and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening.
The committee raised the repo rate and shifting its stance to calibrated tightening.
The committee raises the repo rate and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening.
The committee raised the repo rate and its stance was shifted to calibrated tightening.
questions.e: Parallel verbs 'raised' and 'shifted'; (D) breaks parallelism with passive voice.

questions.subject: CR
questions.q: The World Bank raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 7.1% citing strong Q1 growth of 7.8%. Which would most weaken the forecast?
o: A sharp rise in global crude prices driven by the West Asia conflict
questions.e: Only (A) introduces a downside risk; the rest support growth.

questions.subject: PS

questions.e: 0.25 percentage points = 25 basis points (1 bp = 0.01%).

questions.subject: RC
questions.q: TRISHNA's primary purpose, according to ISRO, is:
questions.e: Thermal infra-red imaging for water resources; open-data policy.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The laureates were honoured for their contributions to the IceCube Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos.
The laureates were honoured for their contributions to the IceCube Observatory and discovering high-energy neutrinos.
The laureates were honoured for contributing to the IceCube Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos.
The laureates were honoured for their contributions to the IceCube Observatory and for the discovery of high-energy neutrinos.
questions.e: Parallel nouns 'contributions' and 'discovery'; (D) adds an unnecessary 'for'.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The laureates won for the discovery of light-gated ion channels and the development of optogenetics.
The laureates won for the discovery of light-gated ion channels and developing optogenetics.
The laureates won for discovering light-gated ion channels and the development of optogenetics.
The laureates won for the discovery of light-gated ion channels and to develop optogenetics.
questions.e: Parallel nouns: 'discovery' and 'development' (Medicine Nobel, 5 Oct 2026).

questions.q: India's quantum-secure network reached 1,000 km of a 2,000-km target. Which most strengthens the claim that the network is strategically significant?
o: It already spans half the planned national backbone
It was announced on a weekday
questions.e: Half the 2,000-km target reached (11 Oct 2026) signals scale.

o: Farmer incomes for pulse growers will stabilise
questions.e: Assured procurement under PM-AASHA price support (11 Oct 2026).

The Navy will induct Mangrole, an indigenous anti-submarine warfare vessel built.
The Navy will induct Mangrole, being an indigenous anti-submarine warfare vessel.
The Navy will induct Mangrole, it is an indigenous anti-submarine warfare vessel.
questions.e: Clean appositive; no redundancy (PIB, 10 Oct 2026).

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence about the Literature Nobel:

Carson won 'for her boldly and inventive oeuvre'.
Carson won 'for her bold and inventively oeuvre'.
Carson won 'for her boldness and inventive oeuvre'.

questions.e: Standard assumption question on the 10 Oct 2026 agitation's premise.

questions.q: Shai Hope scored 102* off 45 balls. His strike rate was about:

o: Fewer arrests raise compliance rather than lower deterrence
questions.e: Classic GMAT CR assumption question on the 8 Oct 2026 GST decision.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:

The prosecution threshold were raised from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
The prosecution threshold has been raise from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
The prosecution threshold raised from Rs 1 crore and Rs 5 crore.
questions.e: Singular subject 'threshold' takes singular verb 'was'.

questions.subject: PS
questions.q: The GST general penalty was cut from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000. The percentage cut is:
questions.e: Cut of Rs 15,000 on Rs 25,000 = 60%.

o: Refunds of excess cash balances become automatic, freeing working capital
The Council meets once a year
questions.e: Automatic refunds directly improve working capital — the mechanism cited on 8 Oct 2026.

questions.q: 90% of refunds sanctioned within 3 working days of acknowledgement, and acknowledgement takes up to 10 days. The maximum typical wait is:
questions.e: 10 + 3 = 13 working days under the new 8 Oct 2026 rules.

questions.e: (99 − 90)/90 = 10%. Percentage points ≠ percent.

questions.e: 25 bps = 0.25 percentage points; 5.25 + 0.25 = 5.50.

questions.q: The RBI shifted its stance ___ 'Neutral' ___ 'Calibrated Tightening'.
questions.e: Idiom: 'from X to Y' — parallel structure.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The Nobel committee cited Pillay's 'efforts to promote peace and international law'. The award's reasoning assumes:
o: the citation reflects her actual contributions
questions.e: Standard assumption question: the stated reason genuinely applies.

o: The 2019 pilot on 42 drugs cut prices up to 91%
Drug companies oppose all price controls
questions.e: A prior, similar intervention with large cuts directly supports the forecast.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Is the Sensex fall on 8 Oct above 1.5%? (1) It fell 1,177 points to 71,461 (2) The Nifty fell 371 points
questions.e: (1) alone: 1,177/71,461 ≈ 1.65% > 1.5%; (2) gives no base.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Is India's power-demand addition above 500 TWh by 2030? (1) The addition is 570 TWh (2) Demand rises 6.4% annually
questions.e: (1) alone: 570 > 500 answers yes; (2) alone gives no absolute figure.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Was Titan's Q2 FY27 revenue above ₹450 crore? (1) It grew 25% YoY (2) Q2 FY26 revenue was ₹400 crore
questions.e: Together: 400 × 1.25 = 500 > 450; neither alone suffices.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The government is considering an ATF price stabilisation fund because jet-fuel prices are soaring. Which most strengthens the case for the fund?
o: Airlines have raised fuel surcharges as ATF prices climbed
questions.e: Rising surcharges show the cost pressure the fund would address.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: SC working strength rose from 34 to 37. Is the increase more than 8%? (1) The increase is 3 judges (2) 3/34 ≈ 8.8%
questions.e: Each statement alone lets you compute 8.8% > 8%: (1) with the stem's 34, (2) directly.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The physics Nobel citation credits 'decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory.' Which assumption is required?
o: IceCube's data actually revealed astrophysical neutrinos
Antarctica is the only possible site
questions.e: The prize logic requires that the observatory delivered the discovery.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: Harmanpreet Kaur, ___ stepped down as captain on 6 October 2026, will continue to play.
questions.e: 'Who' — subject of 'stepped down' in the non-defining clause.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: The Maybach S 580e costs ₹3.35 crore. Is that more than ₹3 crore? (1) 1 crore = ₹1,00,00,000 (2) 3.35 > 3
questions.e: Each alone: (1) converts to ₹3,35,00,000; (2) compares the coefficients directly.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: BoB is the second PSB to enter the pension fund business. Which conclusion is best supported?
o: At least one other PSB is already in the pension fund business
BoB is the largest pension fund
questions.e: 'Second' entails a first already exists; the rest overreach.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: C-DAC's Bengaluru centre has 272 of 951 vacancies. Is Bengaluru's share above 25%? (1) 272 × 4 = 1,088 (2) 1,088 > 951
questions.e: Each alone: (1) shows 4 × 272 > 951, i.e. 272/951 > 1/4; (2) states the same comparison. So EACH alone suffices.

questions.e: 238 − 146 = 92.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Is Alipur's AQI worse than Aya Nagar's by more than 50 points? (1) Alipur 238, Aya Nagar 146 (2) 238 − 146 = 92
questions.e: Each alone establishes the 92-point gap > 50.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: AkzoNobel is nearing a >$1 bn sale of its Southeast Asian paints unit to Nippon Paint. Which most strengthens the claim that regional paint markets are consolidating?
o: Nippon Paint is already the region's largest buyer of paint assets
questions.e: An acquirer already buying regional assets supports a consolidation trend.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: A ₹50 lakh loan EMI rises from ₹43,391 to ₹44,186 after a 25 bps hike. Is the increase more than ₹750? (1) 44,186 − 43,391 = 795 (2) 795 > 750
questions.e: Statement (1) alone computes 795, which answers 'more than 750' directly.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Delhi's AQI fell from 187 to 183. Was the fall more than 2%? (1) The fall is 4 points (2) 4/187 ≈ 2.14%
questions.e: Only (2) gives the percentage; (1) alone cannot compare against 2%.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: Economists expect a 25 bps RBI hike because August CPI hit 4.82% and Brent is near $101. Which assumption is required?
o: Inflation, not growth, is the binding constraint on policy
questions.e: The hike logic assumes the MPC will prioritise inflation control over growth support this week.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: The Nobel Assembly ___ the medicine prize to Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel on 5 October 2026.
questions.e: 'Awarded' — simple past for a completed dated event; 'has awarded' would need present relevance.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Pakistan needed 212 off 20 overs. Did they need more than 10.5 per over? (1) Required rate = 212/20 (2) 212/20 = 10.6
questions.e: (1) alone lets you compute 10.6 > 10.5; (2) merely states the same result.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Delhi's Rs 1,789.52-crore traffic project covers 42 corridors. Is the average cost per corridor above Rs 40 crore? (1) 42 × 40 = 1,680 (2) 1,789.52 > 1,680
questions.e: Each alone: (1) gives the Rs 40-crore benchmark total; (2) shows the actual exceeds it. So EACH alone suffices.

questions.subject: GMAT PS
questions.q: The Gandak fell 177 cm to 50 cm below the danger mark. Its record high was how many cm above the mark?
questions.e: x − 177 = −50 → x = 127.

questions.subject: GMAT PS
questions.q: 1,092 adaptive signals are spread over 42 corridors. The average per corridor is:
questions.e: 1092 ÷ 42 = 26.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Did Brent rise more than 2% above $100? (1) Brent closed at $102.25 (2) 2.25/100 = 2.25%
questions.e: Each statement alone establishes 2.25% > 2%.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The DAC accorded AoN for Rs 520 billion in proposals. Which most strengthens the claim that defence procurement will rise?
o: AoN is the mandatory in-principle step before contracts
The DAC met last year too
questions.e: If AoN is the gateway to contracts, the AoN directly enables procurement.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: The gas ceiling rose from $8.90 to $9.89/MMBtu. Was the rise more than 10%? (1) The rise was $0.99 (2) 0.99/8.90 ≈ 11.1%
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives 11.1% > 10%. Statement (1) alone lacks the base $8.90.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Monsoon rain was 759.4 mm = 87% of LPA. Is the LPA above 850 mm? (1) LPA = 759.4/0.87 (2) 759.4/0.87 ≈ 873
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives ≈873 > 850. Statement (1) alone is just a formula.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The Cabinet raised mustard MSP by ₹413/q to shift sowing toward oilseeds. Which assumption is required?
o: Farmers respond to MSP differentials when choosing crops
questions.e: The policy assumes price signals change planting decisions; without it, the hike can't shift acreage.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: The government ___ the deepwater gas price ceiling to $9.89/MMBtu on 4 October 2026.
questions.e: Past-tense event needs 'raised'; 'rise' is intransitive and 'raising' lacks a helper.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: G7's 100-million-barrel release is expected to cool oil prices. This assumes:
o: Extra supply lowers prices, all else equal
questions.e: The price prediction needs the supply→price link; if demand surges in parallel, prices may not fall.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: India won 21 gold of 85 medals. Is the gold share above 20%? (1) India won 21 gold medals (2) India won 85 medals in total
questions.e: Need 21/85 ≈ 24.7% > 20% — both statements together supply numerator and denominator.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: The repo rate is 5.25%. Will a 25 bps hike take it above 5.4%? (1) 25 bps = 0.25 percentage points (2) 5.25 + 0.25 = 5.50
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives 5.50% > 5.4%. Statement (1) alone lacks the base rate.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: India finished 4th because it had more silvers than Uzbekistan, golds being tied at 21. This conclusion assumes:
o: Medal tables rank by golds first, then silvers
questions.e: The standard golds-then-silvers ordering is the unstated rule making 27 silvers decisive.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: The MPC ___ from 5 to 7 October to decide the repo rate.
questions.e: Present-tense scheduled event with singular 'MPC': 'meets'. 'Met' would need a past time marker.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: BofA doubled its hike call to 100 bps through H1 2027. Which finding would most weaken this forecast?
o: Crude prices collapse and CPI falls back below 4%
questions.e: The hike case rests on persistent inflation; collapsing crude and CPI would remove its foundation.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: India scored 211 and Pakistan 192 in the Asian Games final. Was India's margin more than 8% of Pakistan's total? (1) The margin was 19 runs (2) 19/192 ≈ 9.9%
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives 19/192 ≈ 9.9% > 8%. Statement (1) alone lacks Pakistan's total.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: GEC-III's outlay is ₹1,86,405 cr. Is the BESS share more than a quarter? (1) BESS = ₹50,000 cr (2) 50,000/1,86,405 ≈ 26.8%
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives 26.8% > 25%. Statement (1) alone lacks the total outlay.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: NCW argues mandatory paid paternity leave will raise women's workforce participation. Which assumption is required?
o: Childcare duties currently keep some women out of the workforce
questions.e: The argument assumes childcare is the binding constraint; without it, paternity leave can't move participation.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: The Cabinet ___ the ₹1,86,405-crore Green Energy Corridor Phase-III on 30 September 2026.
questions.e: Past-tense event needs 'approved'; 'approval' is a noun and breaks the verb slot.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: India hit 15 sixes to Pakistan's 10, and won by 19 runs. The inference that six-hitting decided the match assumes:
o: Sixes were the main source of the run differential
All sixes were hit by one batter
questions.e: The 5-six gap ≈ 30 runs > the 19-run margin — the inference needs sixes to be the differential driver.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: India won 16 gold medals at the Asian Games (end of 2 Oct). (1) India won 76 medals in all. (2) One-fifth of 76 is 15.2. Was the gold share above one-fifth?
questions.e: 16 gold of 76 total = 21.05% > 20%: 16 > 15.2. Neither statement alone gives both the numerator and the threshold.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: Hockey India announced ₹11 lakh per player after the Asian Games gold. Which assumption underlies celebrating the award as motivation?
questions.e: The celebration assumes awards drive effort; the other options are irrelevant or false (hockey has no official 'national game' status).

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: NVS-03, ___ launch is targeted for 15–20 October, will restore NavIC to four satellites.
questions.e: 'Its' = possessive of the satellite; 'it's' = 'it is'; 'their' mismatches the singular antecedent.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Maruti's September sales rose 24% to 2.36 lakh units. (1) Last September's sales were 2.36/1.24 lakh units. Were they below 2 lakh?
questions.e: 2.36/1.24 ≈ 1.903 < 2 — statement (1) alone computes the comparison.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The rupee slid to 96.3150 as US Treasury yields surged and FPIs sold. Which fact most strengthens the yield explanation?
o: Other emerging-market currencies fell in the same week
questions.e: A shared fall across EM currencies points to a common external driver — surging US yields.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: UPI did 24.07 billion transactions in September 2026 and 24.51 billion in August. Was the month-on-month decline more than 1.5%? (1) 24.07 < 24.51 (2) The reported decline is 1.8%
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives the 1.8% figure, which exceeds 1.5%. Statement (1) alone only gives direction, not magnitude.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: Ishan Kishan scored 80* off 46 balls. Was his strike rate above 170? (1) Strike rate = runs/balls × 100 (2) 80/46 = 1.739
questions.e: Both together: 1.739 × 100 = 173.9 > 170. Neither alone computes the rate.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The Supreme Court ordered CPCB and the Centre to jointly test barium in firecrackers before fixing permitted hours. Which assumption underlies the order?
o: Test results can inform safe usage limits
Courts must ban all pollution sources
questions.e: The order assumes empirical testing can ground a calibrated middle path — neither total ban nor unrestricted use.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: NVS-03 weighs ~2,250 kg. Can a GSLV Mk II launch it? (1) GSLV Mk II lifts ~2,500 kg to GTO (2) NVS-03 targets a geosynchronous slot
questions.e: 2,250 kg < ~2,500 kg capacity answers it; the target orbit in (2) adds nothing decisive.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: Morgan Stanley expects the rupee to reach 97 per dollar by December 2026, ___ from about 91 at the start of the year.
questions.e: 'Weakening': more rupees per dollar means the rupee loses value — a 6%+ slide in 2026.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: India's Asian Games tally: 10 gold, 21 silver, 29 bronze. Is the number of silver medals more than double the gold? (1) 21 > 2×10 (2) Bronze = 29
questions.e: Statement 1 directly compares: 21 > 20, so yes — sufficient alone. Statement 2 alone says nothing about silver vs gold.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: FASTag Annual Pass issuances crossed one crore since August 2025. Which most strengthens the claim that the pass drove adoption?
o: Issuances grew fastest right after the pass launch
questions.e: A surge timed to the launch most directly links the pass to adoption; the others are weak or irrelevant.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: Defeating Pakistan 4-3 in the semifinal, ___ reached the Asian Games final.
questions.e: The participial phrase 'Defeating Pakistan 4-3' must be followed by the doer: 'India, the defending champions, reached...'

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: India won by 124 runs. What was Sri Lanka's score? (1) India's score was 272 (2) Combined score was 420
questions.e: Statement (2) alone gives only the combined score — not the split. Statement (1) alone gives Sri Lanka = 272 − 124 = 148. So statement (1) ALONE is sufficient.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: Apple Pay launched in India with Axis Bank support. Which is an assumption behind 'this will boost digital payments'?
o: Consumers will adopt it beyond the initial bank
Axis Bank is India's largest bank
questions.e: The conclusion needs adoption beyond the launch partner; the other options are extreme or irrelevant.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: On the GMAT Focus Edition, what is the range of the Total score?
questions.e: The Focus Total score runs 205–805 in 10-point steps and always ends in 5. 200–800 was the old GMAT range; 60–90 is the section-score range.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: Each of the three GMAT Focus sections is scored on what scale?
questions.e: Every section — Quant, Verbal and Data Insights — is scored 60–90 in 1-point steps. All three count equally toward the Total score.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: How many questions and how much time does each GMAT Focus section have?
o: Quant: 21 Q / 45 min; Verbal: 23 Q / 45 min; DI: 20 Q / 45 min
Quant: 31 Q / 62 min; Verbal: 36 Q / 65 min; DI: 12 Q / 30 min
Quant: 21 Q / 60 min; Verbal: 23 Q / 60 min; DI: 20 Q / 60 min
questions.e: Focus format: Quant 21 questions, Verbal 23, Data Insights 20 — each in 45 minutes, 64 questions and 2 hours 15 minutes total.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: Which of the following was REMOVED in the GMAT Focus Edition?
questions.e: The essay (AWA) was removed entirely, along with Sentence Correction; most geometry also went. Data Sufficiency moved into Data Insights.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: On which section(s) is the on-screen calculator available?
questions.e: The calculator appears only in Data Insights. Quant must be done by hand — a major reason mental-math fluency matters.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: During a GMAT Focus section, how many answers may you change on the review screen?
o: None — answers lock when you move on
questions.e: You can bookmark questions and change up to 3 answers per section at the review screen — use it only for identifiable errors, not gut-feel flips.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: How long are GMAT Focus scores valid?
questions.e: GMAT scores (Focus and old) are valid for 5 years from the test date.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: What are the GMAT Focus retake limits?
o: At most 5 times in 12 months and 8 times lifetime, with 16 days between attempts
questions.e: You may test up to 5 times in a rolling 12-month period and 8 times total, with at least 16 days between attempts.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: GMAT Focus Total scores always end in which digit?
questions.e: Focus Totals are given in 10-point steps starting at 205, so they always end in 5 (e.g. 645, 705). A score ending in 0 is an old-format score.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: Where do you register for the GMAT and manage score reports?
questions.e: Registration, scheduling, rescheduling and score-report ordering all run through mba.com (GMAC's site); tests are delivered by Pearson VUE.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: Approximately what is the GMAT Focus exam fee at a test centre?
questions.e: The test-centre fee is about $275 (online delivery can cost more in some regions). Rescheduling and extra score reports cost extra.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: Which statement about GMAT Focus section order is true?
o: You choose the order of the three sections
The order is randomised by the computer
questions.e: You select your section order at the start — most test-takers lead with their strongest section to build momentum.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: How much break time is built into the GMAT Focus?
questions.e: There is one optional 10-minute break you can take between sections; the 2:15 testing clock excludes it.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: Is there a penalty for wrong answers on the GMAT Focus?
o: No — but leaving questions blank hurts more than guessing
No penalty and blanks are ignored
questions.e: No wrong-answer penalty, but unanswered questions damage the adaptive score estimate more than guesses do — never leave blanks.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: When did the GMAT Focus Edition become the only GMAT exam?
o: It never did — both versions run
questions.e: The Focus Edition launched late 2023 and fully replaced the old GMAT on 1 February 2024.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: What does the Enhanced Score Report show?
o: Performance by question type, timing and difficulty, plus section percentiles
questions.e: The Enhanced Score Report breaks down your performance by question type, timing, difficulty level and section percentiles — the raw material for a retake plan.

questions.subject: Overview
questions.q: After seeing your GMAT Focus score, you may:

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A recent study found that cities with more bicycle lanes have lower rates of traffic accidents. The researchers concluded that building bicycle lanes makes roads safer for everyone. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens this conclusion?
o: Bicycle lanes were built mainly in cities that already had declining accident rates.
Accident rates fell specifically on roads where bicycle lanes were added, while unchanged roads in the same cities saw no decline.
Many cyclists do not wear helmets.
Traffic accidents also fell in cities without bicycle lanes.
questions.e: B isolates the effect: the decline happened where lanes were added but not on comparable roads without them — ruling out the alternate explanation that accident rates were falling anyway.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Advertisement: 'Our tutoring program raised students' GMAT scores by an average of 60 points. Enroll now and boost your score!' Which of the following most strengthens the claim that the program caused the improvement?
o: Students who enrolled took the GMAT twice with no preparation between attempts.
A control group of similar students who did not enroll improved by only 5 points on average.
The program has been operating for ten years.
questions.e: C provides the key comparison: without the program, similar students barely improved, so the 60-point gain is attributable to the program rather than retesting or maturation.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Pharmacists report that patients who use a weekly pill organizer miss fewer doses than those who do not. The author concludes pill organizers improve medication adherence. Which strengthens this?
o: Patients who bought organizers were already more conscientious about health than average.
In a randomized trial, patients given free organizers missed 40% fewer doses than a control group.
Many patients dislike the look of pill organizers.
questions.e: C is a randomized trial — it eliminates the self-selection problem (conscientious patients choosing organizers) that weakens the observational claim in B.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A company's profits rose 15% after it shortened the workweek to four days. Management concluded the shorter week caused the profit increase. Which most strengthens this?
o: The profit increase came entirely from a one-time tax refund.
Industry-wide profits were flat during the same period.
The company hired 20 new employees that year.
questions.e: C rules out the alternate cause that the whole industry boomed — the increase is specific to this company, supporting the shorter-week explanation.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Researchers claim that drinking green tea reduces the risk of heart disease, citing lower heart-disease rates among heavy tea drinkers. Which most strengthens the claim?
o: Heavy tea drinkers in the study also exercised more and smoked less than average.
The active compounds in green tea were shown in lab tests to prevent artery-clogging plaque.
Black tea drinkers showed no such benefit.
questions.e: C supplies a biological mechanism linking tea to the outcome, bridging the correlation-causation gap. B actually weakens (confounding lifestyle factors).

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A city installed bright LED streetlights and nighttime crime fell 20%. Officials credit the lighting. Which most strengthens this?
o: Crime also fell 20% in a neighboring city that kept its old lights.
The drop occurred only in districts that received the new lights; districts awaiting installation saw no change.
questions.e: C is a natural experiment: treated vs. untreated districts within the same city isolate the lighting effect.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A study links daily meditation to lower blood pressure. Critics note meditators may simply be healthier overall. Which finding most strengthens the researchers' causal claim?
o: Participants randomly assigned to a meditation program showed greater blood-pressure drops than a waitlist control group.
Long-term meditators report high life satisfaction.
Blood pressure varies throughout the day.
questions.e: B's random assignment defeats the 'healthier people choose meditation' objection — the only systematic difference is the meditation itself.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A software firm found that teams using its new code-review checklist shipped 30% fewer bugs. Which most strengthens the claim that the checklist caused the improvement?
o: The checklist is two pages long.
Teams adopted the checklist voluntarily, and the most careful teams adopted it first.
Bug counts were measured identically before and after, and no other process changes occurred during the period.
questions.e: C rules out measurement changes and other simultaneous interventions — the classic alternate causes in a before/after comparison.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Economists argue that raising the minimum wage did not reduce employment, pointing to a state where employment held steady after a hike. Which most strengthens this?
o: The state's economy was booming for unrelated reasons.
Neighboring states without a wage hike saw similar employment trends.
A neighboring state with similar economic conditions but no wage hike lost jobs over the same period.
questions.e: C provides a control: similar economy, no hike, worse employment — suggesting the hike didn't cost jobs (if anything the comparison favors the hike state).

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A museum's attendance doubled after it introduced free evening hours. The director credits the free hours. Which most strengthens this?
o: The museum also opened a blockbuster exhibition the same month.
Evening attendance consists mostly of visitors who had never come during paid daytime hours.
Other museums in the city also grew.
questions.e: B shows the growth came from genuinely new visitors using the free hours — not from existing visitors shifting times or from the exhibition alone.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A survey found that people who drink coffee daily report higher productivity. A blogger concludes coffee boosts productivity. Which most weakens this?
o: Coffee contains caffeine, a known stimulant.
Highly productive people tend to work longer hours and drink coffee to cope with fatigue.
questions.e: C reverses causation: productivity (via long hours) causes coffee drinking, not the reverse. D also weakens, but C more directly attacks the causal arrow.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: After a town banned plastic bags, litter on streets fell 25%. Activists claim the ban caused the drop. Which most weakens this?
o: The ban was popular with residents.
During the same period the town doubled street-cleaning crews and fines for littering.
Plastic bags are a small share of litter.
questions.e: B offers a powerful alternate cause — doubled cleaning and fines fully explain the drop without the bag ban.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A test-prep company advertises: 'Our students' average GMAT score is 720!' Which most weakens the implication that the course produces such scores?
o: Only students who scored above 700 were invited to report their scores.
The course includes 100 hours of instruction.
questions.e: B exposes selection bias: the advertised average reflects only high scorers who chose to report, not typical students.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A nutritionist claims organic vegetables are healthier because a study found organic eaters have lower disease rates. Which most weakens this?
o: The study's organic eaters were wealthier, exercised more, and smoked less than non-organic eaters.
Some organic eaters still got sick.
questions.e: B shows the groups differed in multiple health-relevant ways — the disease gap may come from wealth/exercise, not organic food (confounding).

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A CEO argues: 'Our profits grew after we cut the marketing budget, so marketing was wasting money.' Which most weakens this?
o: Marketing is important for brand awareness.
The profit growth came from a competitor's bankruptcy, which sent us its customers.
questions.e: B supplies an alternate cause for the profit growth that has nothing to do with the marketing cut.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A study of 50 runners found those who stretch before running get injured less. The author concludes stretching prevents injuries. Which most weakens this?
o: Runners who stretch tend to warm up thoroughly and run fewer miles per week than non-stretchers.
Some stretching runners still got injured.
The study was funded by a sportswear company.
questions.e: B identifies confounders (warm-ups, lower mileage) that could explain the injury gap — stretching itself may be irrelevant.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A school's test scores rose after it adopted a new curriculum. The principal credits the curriculum. Which most weakens this?
o: The same year, the school began admitting students through a selective entrance exam.
questions.e: B changes the student population — higher scores may reflect selective admissions, not the curriculum.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: An economist claims tax cuts increase government revenue, citing a country where revenue rose after cuts. Which most weakens this?
o: The revenue rise came from inflation pushing nominal incomes (and tax brackets) higher, not from real growth.
questions.e: B shows the revenue 'increase' was nominal (inflation), not a real behavioral response to the cuts.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A gym claims its members lose more weight than non-members, based on a member survey. Which most weakens this?
o: People who join gyms are already more motivated to lose weight than the general population.
The survey had a low response rate.
questions.e: B is self-selection: motivated dieters both join gyms and lose weight — membership may cause nothing.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: A wildlife group claims a new highway caused a deer population decline, noting the decline began when the highway opened. Which most weakens this?
o: A severe disease outbreak struck the deer population the same year the highway opened.
questions.e: B offers a competing cause timed exactly with the decline — the highway may be coincidental.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Argument: 'We should build the new factory in Riverton because land there is cheaper than in Milltown.' The argument assumes that:
o: Riverton has a larger population than Milltown.
Land cost is the only relevant factor in choosing the factory site.
Other costs (labor, transport, taxes) will not outweigh the land savings in Riverton.
questions.e: Negate C: if other costs DID outweigh the land savings, the conclusion (build in Riverton) collapses. The argument doesn't assume land is the only factor (B is too strong) — just that nothing reverses the advantage.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: 'This software will cut our accounting costs because it automates invoice processing.' The argument assumes:
o: Invoice processing is currently done manually.
The cost of invoice processing is a significant part of accounting costs, and the software's price won't exceed the savings.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Quant gives 21 questions in 45 minutes. Your average time per question should be about:
questions.e: 45 ÷ 21 ≈ 2.14 minutes per question — budget ~2 minutes.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Verbal gives 23 questions in 45 minutes. Your per-question budget is about:
questions.e: 45 ÷ 23 ≈ 1.96 minutes — about 2 minutes each.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Data Insights gives 20 questions in 45 minutes. Your per-question budget is about:
questions.e: 45 ÷ 20 = 2.25 minutes per question — DI questions get slightly more time.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: You have spent 3.5 minutes on a Quant question with no clear path. The best move is:
o: Keep going — a solve is worth it
questions.e: There is no blank option on the GMAT and sunk time kills later questions. Guess and bank the time.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The GMAT Focus lets you review answers. How many questions can you change per section?
questions.e: You may change up to 3 answers per section during review — flag shaky ones as you go.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: A good flagging strategy is to mark a question for review when:
o: You narrowed to two choices or guessed
questions.e: Flag questions where you guessed or were torn — those are the only ones worth your 3 changes.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: With 10 minutes left in Quant and 8 questions remaining, you should:
o: Work 4 carefully and guess the rest
questions.e: A mix maximizes expected score: secure points where you can solve, guess where you can't.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: On the adaptive GMAT, the first several questions matter more because:
o: They set your initial ability estimate, which later questions refine
questions.e: The algorithm starts with a wide ability range and narrows it — early answers anchor the estimate, so avoid careless errors early.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Which is the better time-check rhythm for a 45-minute section?
o: Check at the halfway mark and with 10 minutes left
questions.e: Two or three planned checkpoints keep you on pace without clock anxiety.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: You finish a section with 5 minutes left. Best use of the time?
questions.e: Use review time on flagged questions only — you get at most 3 changes, so spend them where they count.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: For a Reading Comprehension passage with 4 questions, a reasonable total time budget is:
questions.e: About 2–3 min to read + ~1.5–2 min per question ≈ 6–8 minutes total.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: When two answer choices remain and time is short, you should:
o: Pick based on your best reasoning and move on
questions.e: There is no pattern to exploit; your best judgment beats superstition, and moving on saves the section.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The calculator is available:
questions.e: GMAT Focus provides an on-screen calculator only in the Data Insights section.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Which section order strategy is allowed on the GMAT Focus?
questions.e: You select your section order at the start — put your strongest section where you'll be freshest, or your weakest first to get it over with.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: You get a 10-minute break. When does it occur?
o: Between the second and third sections
questions.e: One optional 10-minute break comes after the second section — plan water, snack, and a reset.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: A Data Sufficiency question is taking long. The fastest path is usually to:
o: Test statement (1), then (2), then together — in that order, stopping when answered
questions.e: The AD/BCE decision tree is designed for speed: test each statement alone first; combine only if needed.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: For Critical Reasoning, the highest-yield pre-reading habit is:
o: Identify the conclusion before reading the question
questions.e: Knowing the conclusion first lets you instantly classify the question type and predict the answer.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: If you fall 5 minutes behind pace in Verbal, the best recovery is:
o: Take one strategic guess on a hard question to reset the clock
questions.e: One deliberate guess buys back ~2 minutes; a small sacrifice now prevents a cascade of rushed errors.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: On two-part analysis questions, a common time trap is:
o: Solving both parts independently when one part's answer determines the other
questions.e: Many two-part questions are linked — solving Part A often hands you Part B. Look for the dependency.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The best way to use the final week before the GMAT is:
o: Light review, timed mixed sets, and full mocks
questions.e: The final week is for consolidation and stamina: timed sets, error-log review, and 1–2 full mocks — not new material.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: During a mock, you should replicate test day by:
o: Strict timing, same breaks, same section order
questions.e: Mocks only predict performance when conditions match: strict timing, real breaks, chosen order.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Which error-log habit most improves pacing?
o: Logging wrong answers with time spent and error type
questions.e: Time + error-type data reveals whether you're slow (technique) or inaccurate (concept) — different fixes.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: A 'time sink' question is best identified by:
o: Spending 60+ seconds with no setup progress
questions.e: The 60-second rule: if you haven't set up a path by then, guess and move — the question has beaten you.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: For Data Insights, the most common pacing mistake is:
questions.e: DI rewards estimation and elimination; precise calculation on every question burns the 2.25-min budget.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Your target score needs ~70% accuracy. The implication for guessing is:
o: Guess freely on the hardest 10–15% to protect time for the rest
questions.e: Strategic guesses on questions you'd likely miss anyway convert wasted minutes into points elsewhere.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The GMAT Focus total score range is:
questions.e: GMAT Focus scores run 205–805 in 1-point increments, always ending in 5.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Each of the three section scores ranges from:
questions.e: Quant, Verbal, and Data Insights are each scored 60–90 and weighted equally.

o: A valid government-issued photo ID matching your registration name
Your passport plus a utility bill
questions.e: You need a valid government-issued photo ID whose name exactly matches your registration; a name mismatch can bar you from testing.

questions.e: The fee is about $275 (varies slightly by region).

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: How soon after the test do you receive your official score?
questions.e: Official scores are typically available within 3–5 days.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: What is the retake policy for the GMAT?
o: Up to 5 times in 12 months and 8 times lifetime, at least 16 days apart
questions.e: You may retake up to 5 times in a rolling 12 months and 8 times total, with 16 days between attempts.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: On test day, you must bring:
o: Valid photo ID matching your registration
questions.e: A valid government photo ID is required; everything else (calculator in DI, scratch materials) is provided or prohibited.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: What should you do the evening before the test?
o: Light review, pack ID and snacks, sleep early
questions.e: The night before is for rest and logistics — a fresh brain beats one more chapter.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: If a technical issue occurs during the test, you should:
questions.e: Always alert the administrator at once — issues logged during the session can support a retest case.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Score reporting to schools: which is true?
o: You choose which scores to send
questions.e: You control score reporting and can send your best sitting to schools.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The essay (Analytical Writing) on the GMAT Focus is:
o: Removed — there is no essay section
questions.e: The GMAT Focus removed the essay; the three sections are Quant, Verbal, and Data Insights.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: Sentence Correction questions on the GMAT Focus are:
o: Removed — Verbal is now RC and CR only
questions.e: Sentence Correction was removed; Verbal now tests Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: How many schools can receive your score for free at booking?
questions.e: You can select up to 5 programs to receive your scores free when you book.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The best breakfast on test morning is:
o: A familiar, balanced meal you've eaten before mocks
questions.e: Eat what worked during your mocks — test day is not the time for dietary experiments.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: When should you arrive at the test center?
questions.e: Arrive at least 30 minutes early for check-in, ID verification, and palm scan.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: During the 10-minute break, the best strategy is:
o: Stand, stretch, hydrate, snack, reset mentally
questions.e: Move, hydrate, and clear your head — and note phones are off-limits in the testing room.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: If you feel a section went badly, you should:
o: Reset and attack the next section — each section is scored separately
questions.e: Sections are scored independently and you choose your order — a bad section doesn't doom the others.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The GMAT Focus replaced the old GMAT format in:
questions.e: The GMAT Focus became the only version on 1 February 2024, replacing the classic GMAT.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: You can take the GMAT:
o: At a test center or online with a human proctor
questions.e: Both in-person test centers and online proctored delivery are available.

questions.subject: Strategy
questions.q: The single best predictor of your test-day score is:
o: Your average on recent full timed mocks
questions.e: Recent full-length timed mocks under real conditions are the most honest predictor — trust the trend.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.e: Statement 1 gives x = 2 or x = -2: insufficient. Statement 2 gives x = 2 only: sufficient. Answer B.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: City X plans to reduce traffic by raising parking fees. Which finding most strengthens the plan?
o: Higher fees in City Y reduced car trips downtown by 15%
questions.e: Evidence that the same mechanism worked elsewhere (City Y: -15% car trips) directly strengthens the causal claim.

questions.subject: GMAT Quant
questions.q: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Probability both are red?

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: Choose the best version: 'Walking to the office, the rain started falling heavily.'
o: Walking to the office, the rain started falling heavily.
While walking to the office, she was caught in heavy rain.
Walking to the office, heavy rain started falling.
The rain started falling heavily, walking to the office.
questions.e: The participial phrase must modify the person walking — only option 2 puts 'she' right after the comma.

questions.subject: GMAT DS
questions.q: What is the value of x + y? (1) x - y = 3 (2) 2x + 2y = 10
questions.e: Statement 1 alone cannot pin x + y. Statement 2 → x + y = 5 directly. Answer B.

questions.subject: Critical Reasoning
questions.q: 35 of 61 economists expect an RBI rate hike. This information most strongly supports which conclusion?
o: A majority of polled economists expect a hike
questions.e: 35/61 is about 57% — a majority of those polled, not unanimity; and expectations are not certainty.

questions.subject: Data Sufficiency
questions.q: Is x greater than 50? (1) x is the number of economists expecting a hike out of 61. (2) x = 35.
questions.e: From (2), x = 35, which is not greater than 50 — sufficient alone.

questions.subject: Sentence Correction
questions.q: Choose the best version: 'The campaign, launched on 2 October, ___ on cleanliness.'
questions.e: The singular subject 'campaign' takes the singular verb 'focuses'.

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.q: The main purpose of a passage describing Special Campaign 6.0 would be to:
o: describe a government initiative and its phases
questions.e: Such a passage reports what the campaign is and how its three phases run — a descriptive purpose.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: RRB NTPC Graduate posts: Goods Train Manager accounts for 2,750 of 3,477 posts. Approximately what percent is this?

questions.subject: Critical Reasoning
questions.q: India won the combined chess trophy while winning neither section's gold. This fact most strengthens the claim that:
o: combined consistency across sections wins the trophy
the trophy is decided by tiebreak
questions.e: The trophy rewards the best combined Open+Women performance — consistency, not a single gold.

questions.subject: GMAT PS
questions.q: A ₹2,00,000 loan at 5.50% simple interest for one year accrues:

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: Harmanpreet Kaur ___ down as captain on 6 October 2026.
questions.e: Past simple with the finished-time marker 'on 6 October 2026'.

questions.subject: GMAT CR
questions.q: The RBI raised the repo rate because inflation was above target. Which strengthens the decision?
o: CPI inflation was forecast at 5.2%, above the 4% target
questions.e: Above-target inflation directly supports a hike.

questions.subject: GMAT PS
questions.q: The World Bank raised India's FY27 forecast from 6.6% to 7.1%. The rise in percentage points is:
questions.e: 7.1 − 6.6 = 0.5 percentage points.

questions.subject: GMAT SC
questions.q: India and Switzerland signed pacts ___ migration and research.
questions.e: 'Pacts on' — the idiomatic preposition.

questions.subject: Critical Reasoning
questions.q: The SME Growth Fund assumes growth-stage SMEs mainly lack:
questions.e: The fund addresses the gap in growth equity for SMEs beyond early-stage and micro enterprises.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The general GST penalty is cut from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000. The percentage decrease is:

questions.subject: Sentence Correction
questions.q: Choose the best version: 'The authority, approved on 6 October, ___ responsible for planning.'
questions.e: The singular subject 'authority' takes 'is'.

questions.subject: Critical Reasoning
questions.q: JOSH teams will do household-level TB outreach. This most strengthens the claim that they will:
o: find TB cases missing from the health system
questions.e: Active household-level case-finding directly targets people outside the formal health system.

questions.subject: Data Sufficiency
questions.q: Is the new GST penalty less than half the old penalty? (1) Old = Rs 25,000. (2) New = Rs 10,000.
questions.e: Both are needed: 10,000 < 12,500, so yes — but only with both numbers.

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.q: The main purpose of a passage on Uttarakhand's literacy milestone would be to:
o: report a milestone and its context
questions.e: Such a passage reports the achievement, the programme (ULLAS) and the sequence of states.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: On 11 October 2026, UNICEF India named Smriti Mandhana its celebrity advocate.
On 11 October 2026, UNICEF India named Smriti Mandhana as its celebrity advocate.
On 11 October 2026, UNICEF India named Smriti Mandhana her celebrity advocate.
On 11 October 2026, UNICEF India named to Smriti Mandhana its celebrity advocate.
questions.e: Correct idiom: 'named X its Y' — no preposition 'as' with 'name' in this construction.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The RBI raised minimum daily CRR maintenance to 99%, effective from the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026.
The RBI raised minimum daily CRR maintenance to 99%, effective for the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026 from.
The RBI raised minimum daily CRR maintenance at 99%, effective from the fortnight began 16 October 2026.
The RBI raised minimum daily CRR maintenance to 99%, effectively from the fortnight begin 16 October 2026.
questions.e: Correct: 'effective from' + date phrase; 'raised … to 99%' with the preposition 'to'.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: In a circular issued on 12 October 2026, the RBI restricted INR non-deliverable derivative contracts for non-residents to hedging purposes.
In a circular issued on 12 October 2026, the RBI restricted INR non-deliverable derivative contracts to hedging purposes for non-residents only applying prospectively.
The RBI restricted in a circular issued on 12 October 2026 INR non-deliverable derivative contracts for non-residents to hedging purposes.
Restricting in a circular issued on 12 October 2026, the RBI's INR non-deliverable derivative contracts for non-residents to hedging purposes.
questions.e: Only the first option places every modifier correctly: the circular's date modifies 'issued', and 'for non-residents' correctly limits the contracts.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The IBCA headquarters, inaugurated on 12 October 2026 at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, serves tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma conservation.
The IBCA headquarters, inaugurated on 12 October 2026 at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, serves conservation of tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.
Inaugurated on 12 October 2026 at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, the IBCA headquarters serves tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma conservation efforts.
The IBCA headquarters serves tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma conservation, inaugurated on 12 October 2026 at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi.
questions.e: The second option keeps the participial phrase adjacent to its noun and the list parallel; the others dangle or misplace modifiers.

questions.subject: CR
questions.q: The RBI restricted INR NDDCs for non-residents to hedging only, tightened rebooking rules and cut the no-underlying-exposure derivative threshold from $100M to $5M. Which finding would most strengthen the claim that the package calmed currency markets?
o: The rupee appreciated 77 paise to 95.05 per dollar in early trade on 13 October 2026 after closing at 95.78 on 12 October.
Global crude prices rose in the same week.
Foreign investors sold Indian equities in October 2026.
The RBI had earlier opened a dollar window for oil companies.
questions.e: The rupee's 77-paise appreciation to 95.05/$ on 13 October 2026 directly evidences calmer currency markets following the package.

questions.subject: SC
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: The Odisha Cabinet has approved free textbooks for about 28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10.
The Odisha Cabinet have approved free textbooks for about 28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10.
The Odisha Cabinet has approved free textbooks to about 28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10.
The Odisha Cabinet has approve free textbooks for about 28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10.
questions.e: 'Cabinet' as a collective noun takes the singular 'has approved'; 'for' is the correct preposition with 'textbooks'.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Optogenetics lets scientists switch individual nerve cells on or off using light. Researchers hope it may eventually help treat epilepsy. Which of the following most strengthens this hope?
o: Epileptic seizures involve abnormal firing of specific neuron populations.
Neurons were discovered in the 19th century.
Light therapy is used for seasonal depression.
questions.e: If seizures involve abnormal firing of specific neuron populations, a tool that switches specific neurons on or off is directly relevant — this most strengthens the therapeutic hope.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q:
Is x > 0?
(1) x² = 16
(2) x³ > 0
questions.e: (1) gives x = ±4 — insufficient. (2) x³ > 0 implies x > 0 — sufficient alone. Answer: (2) alone.

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.q: Neither the government nor LIC was/were willing to retain a majority stake after the strategic sale.
questions.e: With ‘neither…nor’, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (LIC, singular): ‘was willing’.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A merchant marks goods 25% above cost price and then gives a 20% discount on the marked price. What is the profit or loss percentage?
questions.e: Selling price = 1.25 × 0.80 × cost = 1.00 × cost — no profit, no loss.

questions.q: The RBI raised the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50% in October 2026. By how many basis points did it rise?

capsules.subject: Reading
capsules.title: CPI inflation at 5.54% in September 2026 (released 12 Oct)
capsules.body: MoSPI's provisional data released 12 October 2026 put CPI inflation (base 2024=100) at 5.54% in September 2026, up from 4.83% in August. Food inflation (CFPI) rose to 7.74%, with onion inflation at 108.09%; rural inflation was 6.08% and urban 4.88%. WPI for September was due 14 October and the next CPI release is scheduled for 12 November.
